definition: An unsupervised technique for discovering the abstract 'topics' that occur within a collection of documents.
details: Latent Dirichlet Allocation (LDA) is a classic topic modeling algorithm; topic modeling is used for exploratory data analysis, content organization, and understanding themes across large text corpora.

explainer.lead: Topic modeling is an unsupervised technique for discovering the abstract topics that occur within a collection of documents. It matters for exploratory data analysis and understanding themes across large text corpora.

tiers.eli5: It groups a huge stack of documents by what they are about, without anyone labelling them first.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers apply it to organize content and explore large text collections. A pitfall is expecting clean, human-named topics; the output needs interpretation.
tiers.paperLevel: Unsupervised discovery of latent topics; Latent Dirichlet Allocation is a classic algorithm. Limits: results depend on the model and require human interpretation.

explainer.example: An LDA run over news archives groups articles into themes like politics, sports and finance.
